newsitem.title: USA: Alcan urges higher US beverage can recycling.
newsitem.headline: Alcan urges higher US beverage can recycling.

text.p: U.S. aluminum producers should commit themselves to raise recycling rates for beverage cans to 75 percent by the year 2000 from 63.5 percent at present, said Brian Strugell, President of Alcan Aluminum, the U.S. subsidiary of the Canadian aluminum group.
The environmental advantages posed by aluminum packaging no longer offered value to the industry in the current consumer market, he said.

Instead, aluminum producers should position themselves as the economic driving engine of community recycling programs and sell their materials to consumers on the basis of its monetary benefits for financing public projects such as housing.
Sturgell added that the message from the aluminum industry to consumers should be: "It pays to buy aluminum".
He strongly advocated a partnership with charity Habitat For Humanity which would encompass drop off centers for aluminum cans at major retailing outlets.
Sturgell was addressing Alumitech, an industry forum organised by the U.S. Aluminum Association.
